note: m2a-lotpool-1126 (2026-11-26, PREPARED, NOT RUN): Atlas docs/012 M2a. Two jobs on one EA world, master set m1126b, Bin state apex: Trim=0 then Trim=1, each with [MemDiag] AllocSitesOwners at world load and lp* counters. Compare: own heap/virt lines at the load sample (what triggers main-heap cores), lptrim: # lines and lp* counters (Trim=1), pool census by hand (rig pose pool, see job note). Decisions: Atlas docs/012 rows O1b (default), O1c (one idle core = no build), O1d (cores full after load).

jobs.note: [est 18 min] DATA (correctness-grade, not timing), Atlas docs/012 M2a (commit 315fad0): EA world Bridgeport (Baseline-BP-Spring), natural play 10 min, [LotPool] Trim=0, [MemDiag] AllocSites=1 + AllocSitesOwners=1 (own heap/virt lines at the world-load sample = which requests trigger main-heap cores), lp* counters v913 (lpOn lpTrims lpCoresFreed lpFreedKB lpCoresLeft lpKept lpLastUs lpBad; the lptrim: # lines carry the same numbers). [Compat] ApexStandDown=0 because with Apex loaded and ApexStandDown=1 the trim stands down (lptrim.cpp) and AllocSites would need AllocSitesWithApex; same in both arms. RIG POSE READ (manual, not in the queue): at about minute 8 of the job run `python -I tools/memory/ea-pool-census.py` (read-only ReadProcessMemory; pool 0x11CD8B4, whose core list at 0x11CD8C0 is one row: cores, MiB, free %, completely free cores); keep the output in probe-out/. O1c verdict: one core on a busy lot = not worth a build.
